whatItDoes: Computes mean (average), sample standard deviation, sample variance, sum, count, min, max, and range from a list of numbers. Paste a comma-, space-, or newline-separated list and get all metrics instantly.
whyItExists: Most spreadsheets, calculators, and online tools give you either the mean or the standard deviation — rarely all of them at once, with the right formulas. This one uses sample variance (n−1, Bessel's correction), which is what every introductory statistics textbook uses for a single sample. No data leaves your browser.
whoShouldUse: Students doing homework or studying for the AP Statistics or GRE, researchers sanity-checking a calculation, data analysts previewing a small dataset, and anyone who needs quick stats from a list of numbers.
useCases: Compute the average of test scores
Find the standard deviation of a sample to understand variability
Verify variance calculations from a textbook
Get min/max/range of a quick data preview
Compute summary statistics on a small dataset before pushing it to a real tool
Sanity-check Excel or Google Sheets formula results
instructions: Paste or type your numbers into the textarea, separated by commas, spaces, or newlines
Pick a display mode: All metrics (default), or just one
Read the result panel — copy the values you need
Click the result panel to copy a formatted summary
Edit the input to recompute; the parser handles up to several thousand numbers
bestPractices: Use sample variance (n−1) for a single sample, population variance (n) only if you have the entire population
For skewed distributions, prefer the median over the mean — this calculator gives mean only
Round standard deviation to the precision of your data; do not over-report decimals
Verify with a known sample first (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 should give mean 3 and stddev ~1.581)
For large lists, paste from a spreadsheet or text file — the parser handles thousands of numbers
commonMistakes: Confusing sample variance (n−1) with population variance (n) — this tool uses n−1
Using mean when the distribution is heavily skewed or has outliers
Forgetting that standard deviation is in the same units as the data; variance is in squared units
Including text in the input — the parser skips non-numeric tokens silently
Reporting variance when the user asked for standard deviation (common)
Treating the mean as the 'middle' — it's the balance point, not the median
faq: What formula is used for standard deviation? — Sample standard deviation: σ = sqrt(Σ(x - x̄)² / (n−1)). This is Bessel's correction and the default in textbooks and Excel's STDEV.S.

Why use sample variance and not population variance? — Because in practice you almost always have a sample of a larger population. The n−1 divisor unbiases the estimate. If you genuinely have the entire population, divide by n instead.
What happens if I enter text or non-numbers? — The parser silently skips them. The 'Parsed N numbers' counter shows how many valid values were extracted.
What is the maximum input size? — The parser handles thousands of numbers easily. For 10,000+ numbers, expect a brief render pause as the loop runs.
Can I get the median or mode? — Not in this calculator. The most common follow-up is to use a spreadsheet or a dedicated statistics package.
features: Mean, sample variance, sample standard deviation
